title: 5 ways to safely automate OpenClaw with Zapier MCP
summary: Steal these five templates to put OpenClaw to work across your apps with Zapier MCP. Zapier handles the logins, you choose what OpenClaw can run, and repeat work becomes a Zap that keeps running.
body_markdown:
When OpenClaw went viral, the reaction from most people I talked to was some mix of impressed and afraid. The idea that an open-source[AI personal assistant](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-personal-assistant/) could negotiate a car deal or fight your insurance company over WhatsApp while you slept was…a lot to process.


In case you're only tangentially familiar, OpenClaw is made up of two parts—an AI agent that runs on a computer or server you control, and a gateway that lets you talk to it from a messaging app like WhatsApp or Telegram. The agent is powered by an LLM of your choosing, and because it lives on your machine, it can access things like your file system, command line, calendar, and email.


There's also a large community of users who have built skills for OpenClaw, connecting it to various third-party apps. Lots of those skills have been flagged as malicious, though. With an agent that has direct access to your machine, granting the *wrong* access can turn catastrophic pretty quickly, especially if you're using it for work.


That's where Zapier MCP comes in. Add it to OpenClaw and the agent can take real actions across 10,000+


apps in our[directory](https://zapier.com/apps) , while Zapier handles each app's login so OpenClaw never touches your raw credentials. You choose exactly which actions it's allowed to run. And when a task turns into something you ask for every week, OpenClaw can build it into a Zap (an automated workflow) that keeps running on Zapier after you close the chat.


Below, I'm sharing five workflows you can set up today in OpenClaw, each with a template to get you started fast.


**Warning:** OpenClaw is powerful, but it comes with risks. Zapier MCP sidesteps the biggest pitfalls by keeping your automated workflows scoped and transparent. But no matter how you're automating, it's worth understanding the safety risks before you start using it.

## How to connect OpenClaw to Zapier MCP


Before you try these workflows, you'll need to add Zapier MCP to OpenClaw if you haven't already. If you can click, type, and copy-paste, you can set this up in minutes. Just follow the steps below.


**Looking for custom logic or raw API access?** You can also connect your code files to Zapier SDK. Check out our feature guide to[learn the difference between Zapier MCP and Zapier SDK](https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-mcp-vs-sdk/) .


1.


Head to the[Zapier MCP dashboard](http://mcp.zapier.com/) .


2.


Click **+New MCP Server** and choose **OpenClaw** as the client.


3.


Now set up your first action. Click **+Add tool.**


4.


Search for the app you want to connect to, then click **its corresponding tile.**


5.


Select whichever action events you want to connect, then click **Connect.**


6.


Connect your app accounts as needed.


7.


In the dashboard, configure each action according to your needs by clicking the kebab menu (⋮) and then **Configure** , then adjusting values as needed. Hover over the tooltip icons next to any field for more details. When you're done, click **Save.**


8.


Finally, click **Connect** at the top of the MCP dashboard and follow the instructions to add this server to your OpenClaw account.


Now you're ready to try the workflows below in OpenClaw.


**Pro tip:** Want to bake an extra layer of security into your MCP workflows? Try connecting[AI Guardrails by Zapier](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-guardrails-guide/) , a built-in tool for detecting PII, toxic language, prompt injection attempts, and negative sentiment in your workflows.


## Turn Slack messages into tracked action items


You're a team lead who ends every day with a Slack channel full of decisions, requests, and follow-ups buried in the noise. You want an agent that can read the last 24 hours of messages, use judgment to distinguish real action items from water-cooler chat, and get them into your project management tool—without you having to triage every thread.


Turn Slack messages into tracked action items


Pull messages from Slack, identify action items, and create assigned tasks in Asana automatically


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/turn-slack-messages-into-tracked-action-items)


## Qualify and route new leads from your CRM


You're a sales ops manager who wants new leads in HubSpot triaged and routed to the right rep the moment they hit the CRM—without building a rigid rules engine that breaks every time your ICP shifts. You want an agent that can read the record, make a judgment call on fit, and move things forward.


Qualify and route new leads from your CRM


Score new HubSpot leads against your ICP, update their records, and route high-fit leads to the right rep


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/qualify-and-route-new-leads-from-your-crm)

You're a consultant or account manager who spends too much time after every client call turning raw notes into a polished recap. You want the first draft to exist before you've even closed the meeting tab—formatted, on-brand, and ready to review rather than ready to start.


Draft client-ready reports from meeting notes


Turn meeting notes into a polished recap email and save it to Notion and Gmail as a draft


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/draft-client-ready-reports-from-meeting-notes)


## Monitor competitor content and log key signals


You're a product marketer or competitive intel person who needs to stay on top of what competitors are shipping—but you also need someone to do the reading and tell you what actually matters. You want the agent to search, form a view on what's worth flagging, and log it, so you're not staring at a raw feed of links.


Monitor competitor content and log key signals


Search the web for competitor updates, summarize what matters, and log findings to Google Sheets


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/monitor-competitor-content-and-log-key-signals)


## Push research summaries from the web into your project tracker


You're a strategist, researcher, or content lead who regularly kicks off projects with a round of desk research—and you want that research to land somewhere useful instead of dying in a browser tab. You want OpenClaw to do the searching, synthesize what it finds, and drop a structured summary directly into your workflow.


Push research summaries from the web into your project tracker


Search the web for market research, synthesize findings, and create a structured brief in Asana


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/push-research-summaries-from-web-into-project-tracker)


## Turn what you repeat into a Zap


Asking OpenClaw to do something once is a good way to test it. When you catch yourself sending the same request every day, ask it to build a Zap instead: "Whenever a new lead lands in HubSpot, score it against our ICP and route the high-fit ones to the right rep." OpenClaw drafts the Zap and deploys it to Zapier, where it starts when something happens in your apps, like a new CRM record or a Slack message, or on a schedule you set. It no longer waits for you to message the agent from WhatsApp, and because it runs on Zapier instead of your own machine, it keeps working when your computer is off.


A few things make it hold up:


-


**The same result every time.** A Zap uses AI only in the steps that call for judgment, like deciding whether a lead is a fit. Everything around that step, like updating the record or posting to Slack, is a regular step that runs the same way each time.


-


**It fixes what breaks.** Every run is logged. When one fails, Zapier works out what went wrong and proposes a fix you can approve, or talk through with OpenClaw.


-


**It gets cheaper and sturdier.** When an AI step ends up doing the same thing on every run, Zapier can offer to swap it for a regular step: same result, fewer tokens.


## OpenClaw and Zapier FAQ


### Why use Zapier for OpenClaw automation?


Zapier makes OpenClaw do more—and more securely. Community skills vary in quality, and some have been flagged as malicious. With Zapier MCP, one connection reaches 10,000+


apps, Zapier handles the logins, and you pick which actions OpenClaw can run. The Zaps it builds keep running after the chat ends, and if one breaks, Zapier proposes the fix.


### Can't I just have OpenClaw run this on a schedule?


You can, but it's the long and expensive way. The agent works through every step each time, on a machine that has to stay on. A Zap starts when something happens, like a new lead or a new Slack message, or on a schedule, and uses AI only in the steps that need it. It runs when it's triggered, gives you a consistent result, and costs less.


### Why not have OpenClaw write me a script?


You can, and it may work on the first try. The trouble shows up later. A script needs somewhere to run, a way to hear about new events, and someone to keep it going. When an API changes or a login expires, it quietly stops until you notice. It also holds your keys, often on the same machine OpenClaw already has the run of. With Zapier, OpenClaw builds the Zap, Zapier hosts it and runs it on real triggers, and keeps your connections working. When something breaks, Zapier finds the problem and proposes the fix, and you approve it.


## Start building with Zapier MCP


These five workflows are a starting point. Once OpenClaw is connected to your tools through Zapier MCP, you can chain together almost any sequence of research, decision, and action across all of your business-critical apps. Zapier is where that work keeps running, and OpenClaw gets access to your apps, not your keys: you pick which apps and actions it can use, and Zapier manages the logins. If you don't use OpenClaw, you can connect Zapier MCP to any other AI tool that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), including[Claude](https://zapier.com/blog/automate-claude-zapier-mcp/) , ChatGPT, and Cursor.
